name: Question 2
problem:
Given that

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+x+1}{{x}^{3}(x+1)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{C}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{D}{x+1},
$$

where $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ are real constants, determine the value of $AB-CD.$
worked_solution:
Multiplying both sides of the given equality by ${x}^{3}(x+1)$ gives

$$
{x}^{2}+x+1=A{x}^{2}(x+1)+Bx(x+1)+C(x+1)+D{x}^{3}.
$$

Letting $x=-1$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(-1)^{2}+(-1)+1 & =A(-1)^{2}(-1+1)+B(-1)(-1+1)+C(-1+1)+D(-1)^{3} \\ 1-1+1 & =-D \\ 1 & =-D \\ D & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=0$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{0}^{2}+0+1 & =A(0)^{2}(0+1)+B(0)(0+1)+C(0+1)+D(0)^{3} \\ 1 & =C.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=1$ and using our values for $C$ and $D$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{1}^{2}+1+1 & =A(1)^{2}(1+1)+B(1)(1+1)+1(1+1)+(-1)(1)^{3} \\ 1+1+1 & =2A+2B+2-1 \\ 2B & =2-2A \\ B & =1-A.\,\,(1)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, letting $x=2$ and using our values for $C$ and $D$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{2}+2+1 & =A(2)^{2}(2+1)+B(2)(2+1)+1(2+1)+(-1)(2)^{3} \\ 4+2+1 & =12A+6B+3-8 \\ 6B & =12-12A \\ B & =2-2A.\,\,(2)\end{aligned}
$$

From $(1)$ and $(2)$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}1-A & =2-2A \\ A & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute the value of $A$ into $(1)$  to get the value of $B:$

$$
B=1-1=0
$$

Finally,

$$
AB-CD=1(0)-1(-1)=1.
$$

EXPLANATION

Multiplying both sides of the given equality by x3(x+1) gives x2+x+1=Ax2(x+1)+Bx(x+1)+C(x+1)+Dx3.

Letting x=−1 gives (−1)2+(−1)+1=A(−1)2(−1+1)+B(−1)(−1+1)+C(−1+1)+D(−1)31−1+1=−D1=−DD=−1.

Letting x=0 gives 02+0+1=A(0)2(0+1)+B(0)(0+1)+C(0+1)+D(0)31=C.

Letting x=1 and using our values for C and D gives 12+1+1=A(1)2(1+1)+B(1)(1+1)+1(1+1)+(−1)(1)31+1+1=2A+2B+2−12B=2−2AB=1−A.(1)

Now, letting x=2 and using our values for C and D gives 22+2+1=A(2)2(2+1)+B(2)(2+1)+1(2+1)+(−1)(2)34+2+1=12A+6B+3−86B=12−12AB=2−2A.(2)

From (1) and (2) we have 1−A=2−2AA=1.

Now we substitute the value of A into (1) to get the value of B: B=1−1=0

Finally, AB−CD=1(0)−1(−1)=1.
